questions.q: Per this lesson, what are the four questions a governance dashboard needs to answer for the program as a whole?
options: Is it on track, where is it off track, is it trending the right way, and who owns each item
What color scheme to use, which font to use, how many tiles to show, and what chart type to pick
Who built the dashboard, when it was built, how much it cost, and who approved it
What software it runs on, who licenses it, how often it's patched, and who administers it
questions.explain: The lesson defines these four questions as what a governance dashboard needs to answer, mirroring what a single KPI answers but at the program level.

questions.q: What does the lesson say about Power BI's Goals feature in relation to data governance?
options: It wasn't built for governance specifically, but its current value / target / trend / status structure fits a governance program's needs
It was built specifically as a data governance product
It cannot track more than one metric at a time
It replaces the need for KPIs entirely
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that Goals is a general-purpose feature, used here as an example of the right structure, not a governance-specific tool.

questions.q: In the screenshot of the goal-editing pane, which fields are shown for a single tracked goal?
options: Owners, current value, final target, status, start date, and due date
Only a goal name and nothing else
A list of SQL queries
A list of every employee in the company
questions.explain: The guide describes the goal-edit pane showing Owners, Current value, Final target, Status, Start date, and Due date.

questions.q: What design habit does the lesson recommend for a dashboard's status thresholds?
options: They should match the thresholds the escalation process from earlier lessons actually uses
They should be set randomly each quarter
They should always be set to 100%
They don't need to match anything else in the program
questions.explain: The lesson warns that a dashboard disagreeing with the thresholds people use to triage issues erodes trust.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say a governance dashboard should keep its headline level small (five to ten metrics)?
options: So a steering committee can actually read it in under a minute, with drill-down available for anyone who wants more detail
Because BI tools can't render more than ten tiles
Because governance programs only ever track five to ten things total
Because larger dashboards are against company policy everywhere
questions.explain: The lesson's design habits call for a small headline set with drill-down underneath, not a hard technical limit.
